items.q: Does using longer, more complex words always improve writing?
items.correct: No — clear, precise words that suit purpose and audience matter more.
items.misconception: Yes, the longer the words the better.
items.why: Good writing matches vocabulary and sentence variety to purpose and audience, not just length.

items.q: What is an apostrophe used for?
items.correct: To show possession or omission (contractions like don't).
items.why: Apostrophes mark ownership (the dog's bone) or missing letters — not plurals.

items.q: What does analysing a non-fiction text involve?
items.correct: Examining how language and structure achieve the writer's purpose.
items.misconception: Just summarising what the text says.
items.why: Analysis explains the effect of word choice, tone and structure on the reader.
